slowdown.note: Original co-sponsor (not his own statement) of H.R. 10538, the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act of 2026, whose Section 8 puts every advanced AI system under a 'mandatory pause' until a new federal Department of Artificial Intelligence is staffed and has issued rules; a pause for safety reasons counts as yes here.

pause.note: Co-sponsor of H.R. 10538; the bill's mandatory pause on advanced AI is conditional on the new department issuing safety rules, which the rubric treats as mixed. No statement of his own found.

intl.note: H.R. 10538 (Section 15) directs pursuit of international agreements and allied coordination to prevent artificial superintelligence, but does not name China or talks with China on pacing; nothing else found.

rsi.note: Co-sponsor of H.R. 10538. Beyond banning superintelligence, the bill's Section 9(a) prohibits AI systems showing 'superintelligence precursor characteristics', which include 'The capacity to automate or greatly accelerate the process of artificial intelligence research and development', and its pause covers training 'including through recursive self-improvement'. This reading comes from the bill text and a reviewer should confirm it; another co-sponsor's file (Velázquez) set this to none based on news reports only.

record: Original co-sponsor of H.R. 10538, the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act of 2026 (introduced by Rep.
